source: G7 World, part A (GROUND.md §6.8): Rust's loot economy and progression with our names. Salvage is our scrap, the currency. Barrels break and spill their loot; crates are looted and go once empty; both come back on a timer (Rust's spawn groups refill in about 20 to 45 minutes). The recycler returns about half of a crafted item's recipe (Rust's 50%) and fixed salvage and materials for loot-only components (Rust's recycler table: gears 10 scrap and 13 metal fragments, springs 10 and one HQM, pipes 5 and one HQM, tech trash 20 and one HQM, blades 2 and 15 fragments, sheet metal 8, 100 fragments and one HQM, road signs 5 and one HQM, the semi body 15, 75 fragments and two HQM, the rifle body 25 and two HQM), one batch every 5 s, a tenth of a stack at a time. Research tables take 10 s and Rust's scrap prices by tier (20, 75, 125, 500). Tech trees: one per workbench level, Rust's layout and scrap costs in kind, each node needing one of the nodes before it; a recipe in no tree is known from the start (Rust's default blueprints). Teams of 8 (Rust's default), invites last 5 minutes. Up to 5 map markers. Loot spots: deterministic clusters of barrels and a crate along coasts and forest edges over the whole world (and some in the open), never within 90 m of the landing site. One recycler stands on each cube face of the world.

techTrees.note: CRAFT-01/04: an unlevelled tree, distinct from standard workbench speed. Tin Finch's 500 salvage is provisional balance.
CRAFT-01/02: separate unlevelled tree; technologies remain undefined in the design, so none are invented here.

loot.note: One candidate cluster per cube-sphere cell of the level nearest 'cell' metres, over the whole world (docs/WHOLE_WORLD.md §7.2), never within 'clear' of the landing site, kept by what is around it: the sea within 35 m (coast), a forest edge (trees near but not on the spot, or forest and open biomes side by side), or open ground. 'landing' is a cluster always kept near the landing site (metres east, unused, south of it), so arrivals there find loot.

recyclers.note: One recycler on each of the world's six cube faces, on the face's first coastal cell with room, else its first with room (docs/WHOLE_WORLD.md decision 9).

map.note: The map is the whole world (docs/WHOLE_WORLD.md §11): its grid has as many cells of about this many metres a side on each cube face as fit (25 of 151 m on the first world), named by face and by Rust's cell, "C K12".
